Harry Styles concerts on Saturday 12 and Sunday 13 December at Accor Stadium. Show starts from 6pm.

Olympic Park will be very busy on Saturday and Sunday with around 80,000 Harry Styles fans expected each night, as well as 20,000 additional fans attending other events in the precinct across the weekend. 

Motorists should allow plenty of extra travel time on roads approaching Olympic Park including the M4 Mwy, Homebush Bay Dr, Concord Rd, Lane Cove Rd, Parramatta Rd, Centenary Dr and Silverwater Rd.

  • PARKING: Car parks will be in high demand and are likely to sell out in advance, fans are urged to pre-book parking online ahead of time to secure a space. A flat rate $40 parking fee applies. 
  • If you have pre-booked your parking, follow the directions of staff and have your parking ticket ready to show at the car park entry. If you haven't pre-booked parking don't drive to Olympic Park.
  • Carpool with your group and allow plenty of extra travel time as traffic will be heavy.
  • Alternatively, consider parking at a nearby train station commuter car park and continuing your trip by train to Olympic Park, at no extra cost.

Sydney Olympic Park Authority will close local roads in the precinct and traffic congestion is expected before and after the concert. For road closure details, visit the Sydney Olympic Park Authority interactive map.

A-League Women: Sydney FC v Canberra United at Sydney Olympic Park Athletic Centre on Saturday 21 November. Game starts at 5pm.

Olympic Park will be very busy with thousands of people also travelling to concerts in the precinct.

Motorists should carpoll with their group and allow plenty of extra travel time on roads including the M4 Mwy, Homebush Bay Dr, Concord Rd, Lane Cove Rd, Parramatta Rd, Centenary Dr and Silverwater Rd.

Parking is in high demand so pre-book online in advance to secure a space, available until 11:59pm the night before the event unless sold out prior. If you have pre-booked your parking, follow the directions of staff and have your parking ticket ready to show at the car park entry.

Road closures

Sydney Olympic Park Authority may close some local roads to accommodate increased public transport services and ensure pedestrian safety during events. For road closure details, visit the Sydney Olympic Park interactive map for more details.

Road closures are in place as up to 6,000 people are expected to take part in the annual Walk with Christ Religious Procession which will travel from Martin Place to St Mary's Cathedral.

Road closures are in place until 4:30pm, while special event clearways are in effect since 1pm until 4pm

Traffic will be heavy in the city while roads are closed. Motorists should avoid unnecessary travel through the city where possible or allow plenty of extra travel time.

Road closures:

  • CLOSED**From 2pm to 4:30pm: Pitt St between Bridge St and Martin Pl.
  • CLOSED**From 2:15pm to 4:30pm sections of O'Connell, Bligh, Spring, Castlereagh, Phillip, King, Elizabeth, George and Hunter Streets will close.
  • **CLOSED 2:50pm to 4:30pm sections of College St, Macquarie St, Prince Albert Rd and St James Rd will close.

Special event clearways are in effect since 1pm until 4pm on sections of College, Hunter, Macquarie and Pitt Streets. Clearways are strict no-parking zones and apply even to local residents and Mobility Scheme Permit Holders. Check signs carefully before parking as vehicles left in clearways will be towed and a fee applies.

The Singleton Bypass Community Open Day will be held from 10am to 3pm on Sunday 22 November.

Traffic will be heavier than usual as the community travel to and from the open day. Traffic controllers will be on site to direct motorists.

Parking is available at Rose Point Park with staff on site to direct visitors to the main entry point near the Putty Road interchange.

Motorists should allow extra travel time and be aware of increased pedestrian activity on local and surrounding roads.
